title: Gumbo
subtitle: Louisiana stew with chicken, sausage, and prawns
excerpt: Gumbo is a rich, dark stew built on a slow-cooked roux. Chicken, sausage, and prawns all go in together with peppers and celery. Serve it over rice for a filling, deeply flavoured meal.
sourceNotes: Gumbo is the official state dish of Louisiana, drawing on West African, French, and Native American cooking traditions. The dark roux is its defining technique.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the prawns. Add fresh prawns when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and freeze half.

content.text: The roux is everything in gumbo. Stir flour and oil over medium heat for 20 to 30 minutes until it turns the colour of dark chocolate. Do not rush it and do not stop stirring.

items.prepNote: use andouille sausage if available -- sliced into rounds

content.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the flour all at once. Stir constantly for 20 to 30 minutes until the roux is very dark brown, like dark chocolate.
Add the onion, celery, and pepper to the roux. Stir well and cook for 8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Season with cayenne pepper.
Add the chicken pieces and sausage. Stir to coat them in the roux.
Pour in the chicken stock gradually, stirring after each addition. Add the bay leaves and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Add the prawns to the gumbo and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until pink and cooked through. Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Ladle the gumbo into deep bowls over a scoop of rice.

items.cause: Heat too high or stirring stopped
items.fix: Discard and start again. A burnt roux makes the whole dish bitter. Keep the heat at medium and stir constantly.

items.cause: Not enough roux or too much stock
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for another 20 minutes to reduce and thicken.
Add the chicken after the vegetables and check it is just cooked before the long simmer. Boneless thighs are more forgiving than breast.

content.text: Gumbo is the state dish of Louisiana and a product of the region's layered history. West African cooks brought the technique of thickening stews with okra or roux. French settlers contributed the dark roux method. Native American cooks added file powder as a thickener. All of these traditions merged in the bayou kitchens of southern Louisiana over hundreds of years.
